# 1c: qobuz-dl-go

This step happens in `~/projects/qobuz-dl-go`. Its details live there; this contract says what shelf needs from it. qobuz-dl-go splits the work into eleven steps of its own, with contracts in its `docs/build/`; its `docs/status.md` says where they stand.

## Read first

- qobuz-dl-go: `CLAUDE.md`, `UPSTREAM.md`, `docs/requirements.md`, `docs/design.md`, `docs/port-spec.md`, `docs/status.md`.
- The upstream source, `Sei969/qobuz-dl` at tag `v2.5.9`, files `bundle.py`, `qopy.py`, `core.py`, `downloader.py`, `metadata.py`, `utils.py`, `settings.py`, `constants.py`, `exceptions.py`, `db.py`.
- [sources/qobuz.md](../sources/qobuz.md) for the settings shelf uses.

## Done when

- The `qobuzdl` package, the `downloadsdb` subpackage, the `qobuzdltest` fake server and the `cmd/qobuz-dl` CLI exist.
- The golden files generated from Python 2.5.9 pass.
- The `httptest` scenarios pass.
- `make parity` on a multi-disc hi-res album, a CD-quality album and a playlist shows only the differences listed in `UPSTREAM.md`.
- CI on GitHub Actions is green, and `v0.1.0` is tagged and pushed to GitHub, so shelf can require it.

## Decisions

| Topic | Decision | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shape | One Go file per Python file, functions named after the Python ones, a header comment naming the ported file and tag. | Upstream diffs map onto Go files. |
| Types | Inside, API answers stay ordered Python-like dicts, so names and tags see the values as Python does. Outside, typed views (`Album`, `Track`, `Playlist`, `Artist`, `Label`, `SearchPage`, `TrackURL`) carry the fields shelf reads, plus `Raw` with the whole answer. Replaces typed structs throughout; see [decisions.md](../decisions.md). | Byte-for-byte names and tags need Python's types, such as `96` against `96.0`. |
| Templates | `pyFormat`, a port of Python's `str.format` with format specs. Upstream never uses `PartialFormatter`, so the port has none. | Folder and file names must match byte for byte. |
| State | No package-level state. A `Client` holds its `*http.Client`, app ID, secret and token and is safe for concurrent calls; a `DL` holds the client and the options. | Several instances, and tests in parallel. |
| HTTP | The caller passes one `*http.Client` without `Timeout`. The port sets timeouts per call and sends every request through that client, covers and segments included. | A client timeout would cut long transfers; shelf picks the proxy. |
| Playlists | `HandleID(ctx, kind, id, progress)` is `handle_url` without the URL parsing. shelf downloads playlists through it, which writes the m3u8. | `DownloadFromID` writes no m3u8. |
| Progress | `type Progress interface` with release start, track start, byte counts, track end and log lines. A nil sink is allowed. Each download also returns a `*Result` with the final folder and per-track outcomes and delivered formats. | Replaces tqdm and colored logging; shelf records what was delivered. |
| Errors | The upstream exception classes become sentinel errors: `ErrAuthentication`, `ErrIneligible`, `ErrInvalidAppID`, `ErrInvalidAppSecret`, `ErrInvalidQuality`, `ErrNonStreamable`. The port adds `ErrBundle`, `ErrInvalidURL`, `ErrEmptyContent`, `ErrQueryTooShort`, `ErrUnhandled` and `*APIError`, whose body has the token and secrets cut out. Nothing exits the process. | A library must not exit or crash its caller. |
| Files | Folders 0755, files 0644, temp files removed on failure, ffmpeg path in `Options.FFmpegPath` with `ffmpeg` as the default. | Music folder permissions; the segmented path. |
| Test server | `qobuzdltest` serves a fake API and CDN with canned albums, a playlist, an artist and a label, so shelf's 1d tests reuse it. | One fake for both repos. |

## Doc changes

In qobuz-dl-go: `UPSTREAM.md` as ported, `docs/status.md`, `README.md` usage. In shelf: `docs/status.md`.

## Checklist

qobuz-dl-go's step contracts carry these tests, with many more. Golden tests compare against output from Python 2.5.9:

| Edge case | Test |
| --- | --- |
| `clean_filename`: fullwidth characters, separators, empty brackets, NFC, `...` to `…` | `TestCleanFilenameGolden` |
| `get_url_info` on every URL form | `TestGetURLInfoGolden` |
| Folder and track names, including `96` against `96.0`, versions in titles, multi-disc names | `TestNamingGolden` |
| The tag map for albums, tracks, compilations, multi-disc and playlists | `TestTagsGolden` |
| `getFileUrl` and `_modern_sig` signatures for fixed timestamps | `TestSignaturesGolden` |
| Secret derivation from a fixture bundle | `TestSecretsGolden` |

Scenario tests against `qobuzdltest`:

| Edge case | Test |
| --- | --- |
| A multi-disc album lands in `CD 01` and `CD 02` with the right tags | `TestMultiDiscAlbum` |
| A playlist lands in a flat folder with an ordered m3u8 | `TestPlaylistM3U8` |
| With fallback off, a release below the requested quality is skipped | `TestNoFallbackSkips` |
| With fallback on, the delivered format decides extension and tagger | `TestFallbackDeliveredFormat` |
| Demo tracks are skipped and counted as failed | `TestDemoTracksSkipped` |
| A resumed transfer with 206 appends; one answered with 200 starts over | `TestResume` |
| A 404 fails at once; other errors retry with backoff up to 5 times | `TestTransferRetries` |
| `[IN PROGRESS]` becomes the final name, or `[INCOMPLETE]` when a track failed | `TestFolderStates` |
| The segmented path decrypts a synthetic segment and remuxes it | `TestSegmentedPath` |
| A failed track leaves no temp file | `TestTempFileRemoved` |
| An album in the downloads database is skipped | `TestDownloadsDBSkips` |
| A 401 from `user/get` returns `ErrAuthentication` | `TestAuthExpired` |

## As built

qobuz-dl-go `v0.1.0` was tagged on 2026-11-04 at commit `e6861b4` and ports qobuz-dl 2.5.9. `GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org go list -m github.com/tikhonp/qobuz-dl-go@v0.1.0` resolves it. Its `go.mod` says `go 1.27.3`, as shelf's does.

Every line of Done when holds. Every test in the checklist exists under the name given there and passes, along with the goldens and the rest of the suite. CI on GitHub Actions is green. `make parity` ran against Qobuz on Pink Floyd's Ummagumma (2 discs, 24/192), Radiohead's Com Lag: 2+2=5 (16/44.1) and the playlist Top 10 Operas, and every file came out byte for byte the same as Python's, with no allowed differences. A resumed run skipped every track. Given a `qobuz_dl.db` that Python had filled, the CLI skipped the album Python had recorded. qobuz-dl-go's `docs/status.md` lists the runs under Reference albums. No track took the segmented path in those runs, and none of the three items had a booklet. The fake covers both.

What differs from this contract:

- `go.mod` requires `modernc.org/sqlite` for `downloadsdb`. The root package and `qobuzdltest` don't import it.
- The port has no exported version string.
- `GetURLInfo` doesn't accept `/interpreter/` links, and neither does upstream.

### For 1d

- Require `github.com/tikhonp/qobuz-dl-go v0.1.0`. Start from `DefaultOptions()`. Its `Quality` is Python's 6, and the bot runs 27.
- `DownloadResult.Tool` takes the module version from `runtime/debug.ReadBuildInfo` and the qobuz-dl version, 2.5.9, from `UPSTREAM.md`. `ParseLink` maps `/interpreter/` links itself.
- When the token expires, a 401 on `album/get` or `track/get` during `DownloadFromID` is a request error, which Python logs and skips. The call returns no error, and the release has `StatusFailed` with an `*APIError` of status 401 in `Release.Err`. To mark the source unhealthy, look there. A 401 on a playlist's pages in `HandleID` returns `ErrUnhandled`, and `errors.As` finds the `*APIError` inside it.
- `HandleID` on a playlist sends one `ReleaseStart` of kind `playlist`, and a `TrackEnd` for every planned track, as `OutcomeSkipped` when the downloads database already has the track. `Result.M3U` is the m3u8's path. An invalid URL returns `ErrInvalidURL` with an empty `Result` that isn't nil.
- `Progress.TrackEnd` gets the track's path in the work folder, `[IN PROGRESS] <name>` for albums. The `Result` has the final path. `TrackEnd` also fires for tracks that never started because the context ended.
- A failed direct transfer retries on the segmented path in the same tier, as Python does. `TrackInfo.Segmented` marks that attempt. The host needs ffmpeg on PATH or in `Options.FFmpegPath`, or tracks Qobuz serves only segmented fall to the next tier and then fail. A test that wants a track to fail needs `Fail404`, enough `FailTimes`, or no ffmpeg.
- `qobuzdltest`:
  - The checklist's fake-backed tests can use it as it is. `PlaylistEmpty`, `ArtistEmpty` and `LabelEmpty` cover `TestResolveEmptyCollection`, and `ExpireToken` covers `TestHealthTokenExpired`.
  - `ArtistAlbums` is an artist whose albums all download. The recorded `Artist` and `Label` lead to 404s on `album/get`, except for the label's compilation.
  - `Segmented(id)` sends a track down the segmented path. `FailStatic` answers 404 to every cover and goody.
  - `catalog/search` answers the recorded search of each type whatever the query, so a test checks the query through `Requests()`.
  - `Configure` replaces `Options.HTTPClient` with the fake's. Tests of shelf's own client, such as `TestHTTPClientHasNoTimeout` and `TestProxyOptIn`, set `APIBase`, `PlayBase` and `Settings.UserAuthToken` by hand instead, since the fake is plain HTTP on localhost.
- For a manual check, `qobuz-dl dl -q 27 --db <shelf's file> URL` runs what the bot runs. `cmd/qobuz-dl/printer.go` is a small example of a `Progress`.
